applicability.defect: a separate mounting footprint does not conform to a curved host while the upper component must retain its authored shape

preconditions: the component is intentionally separate in the product or prop construction (movable, bolted, clamped, or assembled)
only the contact-footprint vertices should deform
the projection axis and direction intersect the intended host surface
the footprint has enough topology to represent the host curvature
required_observations: component-boundary reasoning: separate assembly versus genuinely continuous transition
object local axes and positive/negative Project direction
grouped and ungrouped evaluated vertex displacement
missed projection vertices, degenerates, signed volume, and visual contact
action_policy: Create a vertex group containing only the contact footprint, not the whole secondary part.
Use Shrinkwrap Project on the local axis that points toward the host and enable only the verified hit direction.
Set the modifier's vertex_group to the footprint group before evaluating; an empty group field applies the deformation to the whole part.
Verify that every intended footprint vertex moved, every ungrouped structural vertex remained fixed, and the evaluated part retained non-degenerate volume.
Reject this strategy when the reference implies a continuous cast/welded surface; use connected topology or an explicit boolean/retopology workflow instead.
success_predicates: all intended footprint vertices move onto the target within the declared offset/tolerance
ungrouped structural vertices have zero displacement
evaluated geometry has zero degenerates and retains meaningful signed volume
controlled visual review shows flush contact without whole-part collapse
failure_predicates: wrong projection direction moves zero intended vertices
empty modifier vertex_group deforms the entire component
whole-part projection collapses volume or creates degenerate faces
the component should be continuous with the host but remains a merely touching separate object
recovery: verify local axes and invert Project direction if no footprint vertices move
restore the explicit footprint vertex group if ungrouped structure moves
increase footprint density only where measured curvature error or visible faceting requires it
change representation to connected topology when component-boundary evidence rejects a separate assembly

sources.description: Three independently captured tutorial observations described vertex-group-scoped Shrinkwrap for conforming a mounting rim/footprint while preserving the rest of a secondary part; see curriculum item #4 and its linked video-study records.
sources.trust_tier: Tier B; visual/video observations remained hypotheses until the Blender transfer experiment

experiments.description: runs/2026-08-15_shrinkwrap-footprint-transfer/ projects the same closed 50-vertex/48-quad mount onto a sphere and cylinder. In both scoped cases all 25 footprint vertices moved and all 25 upper vertices remained fixed; maximum analytic-host errors were below 0.024, with zero degenerates. The unscoped sphere control moved all 50 vertices, produced 12 degenerate faces, and collapsed signed volume nearly to zero. The wrong-direction control moved zero vertices. A fresh process independently verified the saved scene and evidence image.
experiments.limitation: Controlled separate-mount fixtures only; no adaptive typed-runtime use on a real prop yet, and no claim about continuous/welded transitions.

status_note: Mechanism transferred from spherical to cylindrical curvature with preserved upper structure and explicit negative controls. Runtime planning/use on a real assembled prop remains required before RUNTIME_VALIDATED.
